title: Kind of Blue: Sketches Only
description: Sketches instead of charts, scales instead of chords, and a tape machine that lied—Go Deep into jazz's most famous album.

questions.question: Which trumpeter handed his band only sketches—no rehearsals—for the sessions that became 'Kind of Blue'?
questions.explanation: "I wanted a lot of spontaneity in the playing," he wrote in his autobiography. It paid off: the album was certified 5× platinum in the U.S. in 2019, 60 years on.

questions.question: Miles cut those Kind of Blue sketches in Columbia's 30th Street Studio—a converted church in Manhattan—across two dates in what year?
questions.explanation: March 2 and April 22. Side one came from day one; side two, seven weeks later. The room's church acoustics are part of why the record still sounds like a cathedral.

questions.question: On those 1959 Kind of Blue sessions, which tenor saxophonist played alongside Miles—weeks before cutting 'Giant Steps'?
questions.explanation: Cannonball Adderley played alto beside him. Two weeks after the final session, Trane cut 'Giant Steps'—a blizzard of chord changes, the polar opposite of what Miles wanted here.

questions.question: Coltrane joined Miles in what new approach—improvising over scales instead of chord changes—on 'Kind of Blue'?
questions.explanation: On 'So What,' the band rides one Dorian scale for 16 bars, slides up a half step for the 8-bar bridge, then comes home. Pianist Bill Evans helped shape the sound—and wrote the liner notes.

questions.question: Bill Evans's liner notes claimed those modal jazz pieces were each captured in how many complete takes?
questions.explanation: Nearly true: 'Flamenco Sketches' took two complete takes, and the album used the second. The real twist? On day one a three-track machine ran slow, so for decades those tracks played slightly sharp until Sony fixed the pitch in 1992.

easterEgg.title: Japanese parchment
easterEgg.text: Bill Evans's liner notes compare the session to a Japanese art form: paint on thin parchment where one wrong stroke ruins the line. Miles arrived with sketches hours before; deliberation was the enemy.
